governingTextNote: This is the official Bureau of Experts English translation. Per the source document, the governing (authoritative) text is the Arabic original.

articles.label: Article 1
articles.chapter: Part 1: General Provisions
articles.text:
In this Law, the following words and phrases shall have the meanings assigned thereto, unless the
context requires otherwise:
Law: Enforcement Law.
Regulations: Implementing Regulations of the Law.
Council: Supreme Judicial Council.
Ministry: Ministry of Justice.
Minister: Minister of Justice.
Court: Enforcement Court.
Competent Department: The administrative unit within the Ministry or the court entrusted with
carrying out any of the enforcement proceedings in accordance with this Law and the Regulations.
Competent Authority: The public entity in charge of enforcement-related activities.
Authority in Charge of Property Oversight or Registration: The public entity in charge of
overseeing a particular type of property, whether movable or immovable, or registering ownership
thereof, including the public entity in charge of overseeing financial institutions and the public entity
in charge of overseeing the Capital Market.
Competent Force: The police or the security agency in charge of assisting enforcement by using
force.
Direct Enforcement: Execution of an enforcement document the subject of which is an act or
omission of an act.
Enforcement Expenses: Financial obligations arising from enforcement proceedings, subject to
applicable provisions.

articles.label: Article 2
articles.chapter: Part 1: General Provisions
articles.text:
1. The court shall consist of both first-instance circuits and appellate circuits or of first-instance
circuits only.
2. Appeals of judgments issued by first-instance circuits in a court with no appellate circuits shall be
considered by the appellate circuits of a court designated by the Council.

articles.label: Article 3
articles.chapter: Part 1: General Provisions
articles.text:
All competent authorities, including authorities in charge of property oversight or registration, must
comply with court orders and decisions relating to enforcement and its proceedings within a period
not exceeding three business days from the date of notification, unless otherwise provided for in this
Law.

articles.label: Article 4
articles.chapter: Part 2: Jurisdiction
articles.text:
1. Except for execution of criminal penalties and matters subject to the jurisdiction of the courts of
the Board of Grievances, the court shall oversee enforcement and its proceedings, including
compulsory enforcement, and shall decide on enforcement disputes and issue judgments, orders,
and decisions relating to enforcement.
2. Subject to the provisions of Article 9 of this Law, the court shall verify that the enforcement
document satisfies legal requirements without considering the merits of the claim.
3. Referral of enforcement petitions shall be in accordance with the rules set forth in the Regulations.

articles.label: Article 5
articles.chapter: Part 2: Jurisdiction
articles.text:
If multiple garnishment orders against the assets of a party subject to enforcement are issued by
multiple authorities, the garnishee must notify the authority issuing the later order of the earlier order.
The Regulations shall specify the provisions necessary for the implementation of this Article.

articles.label: Article 6
articles.chapter: Part 2: Jurisdiction
articles.text:
1. Notwithstanding the provisions relating to jurisdiction provided for in this Law, the Law of
Enforcement by the Board of Grievances, and other relevant laws, if attachment of assets of a party
subject to enforcement is imposed by two judicial bodies, by a judicial body and an administrative
body, or by two judicial bodies and an administrative body, attachment of all such assets shall be
deemed made for all enforcement petitions. The judicial body issuing the first attachment order
shall oversee the attachments arising from such petitions; the sale of assets; the distribution of
proceeds; and the issuance of judgments, orders, and decisions pertaining thereto, in accordance
with the enforcement law applicable to such body.
2. The Minister shall, in coordination with the Council and the Administrative Judicial Council, issue
rules specifying the provisions and procedures necessary for the implementation of this Article.

articles.label: Article 7
articles.chapter: Part 3: Enforcement Document
articles.text:
1. Compulsory enforcement may not be executed without an enforcement document, which shall be
for a defined and due right. Without prejudice to enforcement documents subject to the Law of
Enforcement by the Board of Grievances, enforcement documents subject to this Law shall include
the following:
a) Final judgments, orders, and decisions, as well as judgments subject to expedited enforcement,
issued by courts of the Kingdom.
b) Arbitral awards issued in accordance with relevant statutory provisions.
c) Settlement agreements and reconciliation documents notarized in accordance with the
Notarization Law or issued by legally authorized entities.
d) Bills of exchange and promissory notes recorded in national electronic platforms. The
Regulations shall provide for the conditions, controls, and procedures for recording bills of
exchange and promissory notes in such platforms.
e) Checks.
f) Contracts and declarations notarized in accordance with the Notarization Law.
g) Judgments and judicial orders, arbitral awards, settlement agreements, and attested documents
issued by a foreign state in accordance with Article 9 of this Law.
h) Contracts and documents that bear the same legal effect of enforcement documents pursuant to
a law or resolution issued by the Council of Ministers.
2. The Regulations shall specify the procedures necessary for the implementation of this Article.

articles.label: Article 8
articles.chapter: Part 3: Enforcement Document
articles.text:
If the right underlying the enforcement documents provided for in Article 7(1)(c, f, and h) of this Law
is contingent upon the performance of an obligation the satisfaction of which cannot be verified from
the document itself, the holder of the right may file a petition with the court for enforcement,
accompanied by a report from an expert entity accredited by the Ministry confirming performance of
such obligation. The Regulations shall specify the provisions and procedures necessary for the
implementation of this Article.

articles.label: Article 9
articles.chapter: Part 3: Enforcement Document
articles.text:
1. Subject to the Kingdom’s obligations under international treaties and conventions, a court may not
enforce a foreign judgment or order except on the basis of reciprocity and upon verifying
satisfaction of the following conditions:
a) The case in which the foreign judgment or order is rendered is not subject to the exclusive
jurisdiction of a judicial body in the Kingdom.
b) No pending lawsuit in the Kingdom is filed prior to the filing of a lawsuit with the same subject
matter in which a foreign judgment or order is rendered.
c) The litigants in the case in which a judgment was rendered were summoned, duly represented,
and afforded the opportunity to defend themselves.
d) The foreign judgment or order is deemed final according to the regulations governing the
competent judicial body issuing the judgment or order.
e) The foreign judgment or order does not conflict with a prior judgment or order rendered on the
same subject matter by a competent judicial body in the Kingdom.
f) The judgment or order does not conflict with public policy in the Kingdom.
2. Arbitral awards issued and settlement agreements concluded in a foreign state shall be enforceable
in accordance with the Kingdom’s obligations under international treaties and conventions, and
upon verifying fulfillment of the conditions provided for in paragraph (1) of this Article.
3. Attested documents issued in a foreign state shall be enforceable upon verifying the fulfillment of
the conditions prescribed by the laws of such state, and on the basis of reciprocity between the
Kingdom and such state with respect to the conditions for enforcement of such documents.

articles.label: Article 10
articles.chapter: Part 3: Enforcement Document
articles.text:
If a creditor refuses to receive payment of a due debt established by an enforcement document, the
debtor may file a petition with the court to compel the creditor to receive the payment; in such case,
the court shall order the creditor to receive such payment, and, if receipt of the payment is not
possible, the court shall establish the same and take the necessary measures to enable the debtor to
discharge his obligation, in accordance with the Regulations. In all cases, costs arising from the
implementation of this Article, if any, shall be deemed enforcement expenses.

articles.label: Article 11
articles.chapter: Part 3: Enforcement Document
articles.text:
Without prejudice to relevant statutory provisions, a petition for enforcement filed pursuant to an
enforcement document may not be accepted upon the lapse of more than 10 years from the due date
of the right underlying such document.

articles.label: Article 12
articles.chapter: Part 4: Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 1: Registration of Enforcement Petitions and Issuance of Writs of Execution
articles.text:
The Regulations shall specify the cases in which the creditor must notify the debtor to satisfy the debt
subject of the enforcement document prior to the filing of the enforcement petition.

articles.label: Article 13
articles.chapter: Part 4: Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 1: Registration of Enforcement Petitions and Issuance of Writs of Execution
articles.text:
1. The competent department shall register the enforcement petition upon verifying that the
conditions provided for in this Law and the Regulations are satisfied, in accordance with the
procedures and forms specified by the Ministry.
2. If the competent department decides not to register an enforcement petition for failure to satisfy
the conditions referred to in paragraph (1) of this Article, the petitioner must remedy deficiencies
within 10 business days from the date of notification; if the petitioner fails to do so, the petition
shall be deemed rejected.
3. If registration of a petition is rejected, the petitioner shall have the right to file a grievance within
10 business days from the date of rejection, in accordance with Article 46 of this Law.

articles.label: Article 14
articles.chapter: Part 4: Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 1: Registration of Enforcement Petitions and Issuance of Writs of Execution
articles.text:
If an enforcement document satisfies legal requirements, the court shall order the party subject to
enforcement to satisfy the obligation therein, and the writ of execution shall be served to said party
upon issuance thereof; if service of the writ is not feasible, it shall be published through appropriate
means, and the service shall take effect from the date of such publication. The Regulations shall
specify the provisions necessary for the implementation of this Article.

articles.label: Article 15
articles.chapter: Part 4: Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 1: Registration of Enforcement Petitions and Issuance of Writs of Execution > Chapter 2: Disclosure of Assets
articles.text:
1. The party subject to enforcement must disclose his assets from the date of service or publication
of the writ of execution in accordance with Article 14 of this Law.
2. If petitioned by the party seeking enforcement and if presumptions exist that the party subject to
enforcement has concealed or fraudulently transferred assets, the court shall order disclosure from
the following:
a) Agents of the party subject to enforcement and persons with whom he has a contractual
relationship of employment.
b) Persons who have financial dealings with the party subject to enforcement, his debtors, and
persons suspected of aiding him.
c) Garnishees.
This shall be limited to the extent necessary to achieve the purpose of the disclosure. The person
required to disclose must comply within a period not exceeding 10 business days from the date of
service by the means specified in the Regulations.
3. The authority in charge of property oversight or registration shall, pursuant to a court order,
provide the court with any information in its possession within a period not exceeding three
business days from the date of notification.

articles.label: Article 16
articles.chapter: Part 4: Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 1: Registration of Enforcement Petitions and Issuance of Writs of Execution > Chapter 2: Disclosure of Assets
articles.text:
The authority in charge of property oversight or registration or the entities under its supervision
pursuant to relevant statutory provisions shall, as the case may be, undertake any of the following:
1. establish or designate a department, or more, to be entrusted with processing orders and decisions
relating to enforcement;
2. establish databases for ownership of movable and immovable properties in accordance with the
Regulations; and
3. enable linkage and integration with the Ministry’s electronic systems relating to enforcement
petitions.

articles.label: Article 17
articles.chapter: Part 4: Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 1: Registration of Enforcement Petitions and Issuance of Writs of Execution > Chapter 2: Disclosure of Assets
articles.text:
Subject to the Kingdom’s obligations under international treaties and conventions, exchange of
disclosure on assets with other states shall be on the basis of reciprocity, to the extent necessary to
achieve the purpose of such exchange, and in a manner that does not undermine national security.

articles.label: Article 18
articles.chapter: Part 4: Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 1: Registration of Enforcement Petitions and Issuance of Writs of Execution > Chapter 2: Disclosure of Assets > Chapter 3: Compulsory Enforcement Proceedings
articles.text:
1. If five business days lapse from the date of service or publication of the writ of execution in
accordance with Article 14 of this Law, and if the party subject to enforcement fails to fulfill his
obligation, compulsory enforcement proceedings shall be immediately initiated against the assets
provided for in paragraph (2) of this Article, unless the party subject to enforcement provides a
bank guarantee sufficient to satisfy the obligation; in such case, he shall be granted an additional
period of 10 business days to satisfy the obligation.
2. Compulsory enforcement against assets shall be carried out as follows:
a) Notifying entities licensed to record credit information of the default in satisfaction of the
obligation.
b) Attaching and enforcing against existing assets and any future income, including any amounts
payable to him by public entities, in accordance with applicable provisions.
3. In addition to the measures provided for in paragraph (2) of this Article, the court may impose a
fine of not more than five thousand riyals on the party subject to enforcement for each day of delay
beyond the date set for completion of enforcement, provided that such fine does not exceed the
limit specified in the Regulations. The court may waive the fine, or part thereof, if the party subject
to enforcement fulfills his obligations. The fine shall not be collected until completion of
distribution of the enforcement proceeds. The total amount of the fine shall devolve to the State
treasury.
4. The Regulations shall specify the mechanisms for implementing the measures provided for in
paragraphs (2 and 3) of this Article.

articles.label: Article 19
articles.chapter: Part 4: Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 1: Registration of Enforcement Petitions and Issuance of Writs of Execution > Chapter 2: Disclosure of Assets > Chapter 3: Compulsory Enforcement Proceedings
articles.text:
1. If the period provided for in Article 18(1) of this Law expires, the court shall, upon a petition by
the party seeking enforcement, impose a travel ban on the party subject to enforcement for a period
not exceeding three years, extendable upon a new petition filed with the court by the party seeking
enforcement, provided that the total duration of the ban periods does not exceed six years. In all
cases, the travel ban shall expire upon the termination of the enforcement petition.
2. A travel ban shall not prejudice the jurisdiction of competent authorities to terminate the residency
permit of a non-Saudi, order him to leave the country, or deport him, in accordance with applicable
statutory provisions.
3. The court shall lift the travel ban in the following cases:
a) If the health condition of the party subject to enforcement requires, based on a certified medical
report, medical treatment outside the Kingdom.
b) If the total amount of the debt or debts subject to enforcement is small, as specified in the
Regulations.
c) If the profession, trade, or job of the party subject to enforcement requires travel outside the
Kingdom.
d) If the travel ban would cause harm to the party subject to enforcement.
e) If the party subject to enforcement discloses assets sufficient to satisfy the debt and no
encumbrance exists that would prevent recovery therefrom.
4. The Regulations shall specify the controls necessary for the implementation of this Article.

articles.label: Article 20
articles.chapter: Part 4: Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 1: Registration of Enforcement Petitions and Issuance of Writs of Execution > Chapter 2: Disclosure of Assets > Chapter 3: Compulsory Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 4: Asset Tracing
articles.text:
1. If the party subject to enforcement fails to comply with the writ of execution after commencement
of compulsory enforcement proceedings, the court shall, upon a petition by the party seeking
enforcement, order the tracing of his assets if presumptions exist that the other party has concealed
or fraudulently transferred assets. The costs of asset tracing shall be deemed enforcement
expenses.
2. To the extent necessary to fulfill the right underlying the enforcement document, the court shall,
upon a petition by the party seeking enforcement, authorize such party to access any information
in its possession relating to the assets of the party subject to enforcement. The court may also order
the authority in charge of property oversight or registration to grant access to information in its
possession to persons entrusted with any of the enforcement proceedings. The Regulations shall
specify the controls necessary for implementation of this paragraph.

articles.label: Article 21
articles.chapter: Part 4: Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 1: Registration of Enforcement Petitions and Issuance of Writs of Execution > Chapter 2: Disclosure of Assets > Chapter 3: Compulsory Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 4: Asset Tracing
articles.text:
1. Upon a petition by the party seeking enforcement and if presumptions exist that the other party
has concealed or fraudulently transferred assets, the court may interrogate or order the competent
department or private entity licensed to trace assets to interrogate the party subject to enforcement
or any person suspected, based on presumptions, of unlawfully receiving assets from his relatives,
agents, debtors, persons with whom he has a contractual relationship of employment or financial
dealings, or persons suspected of aiding him.
2. The person ordered to appear for interrogation pursuant to paragraph (1) of this Article must
comply with such order within a period not exceeding three business days from the date the notice
is duly served, as specified in the Regulations. The court may, when necessary, order that such
person be compelled to appear before the court for interrogation.
3. The court may order the competent authority, or the authority in charge of property oversight or
registration, to trace the assets of the party subject to enforcement and any person suspected of
receiving unlawfully transferred assets, and to provide the court with a report thereon.

articles.label: Article 22
articles.chapter: Part 4: Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 1: Registration of Enforcement Petitions and Issuance of Writs of Execution > Chapter 2: Disclosure of Assets > Chapter 3: Compulsory Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 4: Asset Tracing
articles.text:
The Regulations shall specify the controls and procedures governing the tracing of assets, as provided
for in this Chapter.

articles.label: Article 23
articles.chapter: Part 4: Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 1: Registration of Enforcement Petitions and Issuance of Writs of Execution > Chapter 2: Disclosure of Assets > Chapter 3: Compulsory Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 4: Asset Tracing > Chapter 5: Attachment in Aid of Execution
articles.text:
1. All assets of the party subject to enforcement shall be held as security for his debts as of the date
of notification to satisfy the debt in accordance with Article 12 of this Law or as of the date of
service or publication of the writ of execution in accordance with Article 14 of this Law.
2. Attachment and enforcement against provisionally attached assets shall be effected by the
competent authority, and the garnishee shall notify the authority imposing the provisional
attachment once attachment in aid of execution is effected. The Regulations shall specify the
procedures necessary for the implementation of this paragraph.

articles.label: Article 24
articles.chapter: Part 4: Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 1: Registration of Enforcement Petitions and Issuance of Writs of Execution > Chapter 2: Disclosure of Assets > Chapter 3: Compulsory Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 4: Asset Tracing > Chapter 5: Attachment in Aid of Execution
articles.text:
1. The party seeking enforcement may file a lawsuit to nullify any disposition the party subject to
enforcement made to his assets if it is established that such disposition occurred after the date of
notification to satisfy the debt in accordance with Article 12 of this Law or after the date of service
or publication of the writ of execution in accordance with Article 14 of this Law and prior to the
issuance of the writ of attachment. The court shall issue a judgment against the transferee to nullify
the disposition wholly or partly up to the amount of the obligation stated in the enforcement
document if such disposition is in the form of:
a) gifts or donations;
b) prepayment of debt;
c) contracts and financial obligations not customary for a person in his position, as determined by
the court.
2. Any disposition of the assets subject of enforcement made by the party subject to enforcement
shall be nullified if such disposition is made after the issuance of the writ of attachment.

articles.label: Article 25
articles.chapter: Part 4: Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 1: Registration of Enforcement Petitions and Issuance of Writs of Execution > Chapter 2: Disclosure of Assets > Chapter 3: Compulsory Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 4: Asset Tracing > Chapter 5: Attachment in Aid of Execution
articles.text:
1. Attachment of assets of a party subject to enforcement may not exceed the amount of the debt
claimed, unless the attached asset is indivisible.
2. The court shall determine the assets the enforcement against which would achieve prompt
fulfillment, whether before or after the issuance of the writ of attachment. The Regulations shall
specify the relevant controls.
3. The party subject to enforcement may designate specific assets for enforcement if he proves that
he owns assets in excess of the amount of the debt. The court shall adopt such designation unless
it prejudices enforcement.

articles.label: Article 26
articles.chapter: Part 4: Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 1: Registration of Enforcement Petitions and Issuance of Writs of Execution > Chapter 2: Disclosure of Assets > Chapter 3: Compulsory Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 4: Asset Tracing > Chapter 5: Attachment in Aid of Execution
articles.text:
The following may not be subject to attachment and enforcement:
1. Public funds.
2. The residence occupied by the party subject to enforcement or his dependents or the means of
transportation used by him or his dependents only to the extent required by their needs, the items
necessary to practice his profession or trade, and his personal effects. Assets provided for in this
paragraph may be subject to attachment and enforcement if pledged to the creditor or if they
constitute the very property claimed by the party seeking enforcement.
3. Wages and salaries, except as follows:
a) One-half of the total wage or salary for payment of alimony and child support.
b) One-third of the total wage or salary for payment of other debts.
In cases where debts compete for limited assets, one-half of the total wage or salary shall be allocated
to alimony and child support, and one-third of the remaining half shall be allocated to other debts
and, if there are multiple creditors, such amount shall be distributed among them.
4. Civil and military pensions, except as follows:
a) One-half of the total pension for payment of alimony and child support.
b) One-quarter of the total pension for payment of other debts.
In cases where debts compete for limited assets, one-half of the total pension shall be allocated to
alimony and child support, and one-quarter of the remaining half shall be allocated to other debts and,
if there are multiple creditors, such amount shall be distributed among them.
5. Government subsidies to the party subject to enforcement.
6. Any assets exempted pursuant to a resolution by the Council of Ministers.
The Regulations shall specify the provisions and procedures necessary for the implementation of
paragraphs (1, 2, 3, 4, and 5) of this Article.

articles.label: Article 27
articles.chapter: Part 4: Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 1: Registration of Enforcement Petitions and Issuance of Writs of Execution > Chapter 2: Disclosure of Assets > Chapter 3: Compulsory Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 4: Asset Tracing > Chapter 5: Attachment in Aid of Execution
articles.text:
1. The authority in charge of property oversight or registration must promptly enforce the attachment
ordered by the court.
2. If enforcement requires the use of force, the court may order the competent force to execute the
enforcement.
3. The Regulations shall specify the procedures for the attachment, deposit, management, and
receivership of assets, including procedures for attachment of assets due to the debtor in the future.

articles.label: Article 28
articles.chapter: Part 4: Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 1: Registration of Enforcement Petitions and Issuance of Writs of Execution > Chapter 2: Disclosure of Assets > Chapter 3: Compulsory Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 4: Asset Tracing > Chapter 5: Attachment in Aid of Execution
articles.text:
If the court has evidence or presumptions that the party subject to enforcement or another person has
engaged in criminal conduct by concealing, fraudulently transferring, or dissipating the assets subject
of enforcement, or by providing to the court misleading or incorrect information, the court shall refer
the matter to the competent authority in charge of investigation to take necessary legal action in
accordance with applicable statutory provisions; this shall not prejudice enforcement proceedings.

articles.label: Article 29
articles.chapter: Part 4: Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 1: Registration of Enforcement Petitions and Issuance of Writs of Execution > Chapter 2: Disclosure of Assets > Chapter 3: Compulsory Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 4: Asset Tracing > Chapter 5: Attachment in Aid of Execution > Chapter 6: Sale of Attached Assets
articles.text:
The court may allow a party subject to enforcement to sell his assets to the extent that serves the
purposes of enforcement. The Regulations shall specify the relevant provisions.

articles.label: Article 30
articles.chapter: Part 4: Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 1: Registration of Enforcement Petitions and Issuance of Writs of Execution > Chapter 2: Disclosure of Assets > Chapter 3: Compulsory Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 4: Asset Tracing > Chapter 5: Attachment in Aid of Execution > Chapter 6: Sale of Attached Assets
articles.text:
1. Except in the case provided for in Article 29 of this Law and as specified in the Regulations,
attached assets shall be sold by public auction.
2. The sale contract shall be deemed concluded with full legal effect upon issuance of the decision
awarding the auction to the winning bidder.
3. No claims may be raised against the winning bidder regarding sold items for which an award
decision has been issued.
4. Securities subject to the Capital Market Law shall be sold in accordance with controls agreed upon
with the authority in charge of overseeing the Capital Market in a manner that ensures fair pricing
and compliance with enforcement safeguards.
5. The Regulations shall specify the provisions necessary for the implementation of paragraphs (1,
2, and 3) of this Article.

articles.label: Article 31
articles.chapter: Part 4: Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 1: Registration of Enforcement Petitions and Issuance of Writs of Execution > Chapter 2: Disclosure of Assets > Chapter 3: Compulsory Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 4: Asset Tracing > Chapter 5: Attachment in Aid of Execution > Chapter 6: Sale of Attached Assets
articles.text:
1. Sale proceeds shall not be delivered to the party seeking enforcement or his representative except
upon completion of ownership transfer procedures by the competent authority.
2. An occupant of a real property shall vacate such property if requested by the person to whom
ownership of the property is transferred in accordance with this Chapter, unless he occupies it
pursuant to an enforcement document conferring a right to utilize the property. In the event the
occupant refuses to vacate the property, the court shall take the measures set forth in Article 36 of
this Law if petitioned by the new owner.

articles.label: Article 32
articles.chapter: Part 4: Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 1: Registration of Enforcement Petitions and Issuance of Writs of Execution > Chapter 2: Disclosure of Assets > Chapter 3: Compulsory Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 4: Asset Tracing > Chapter 5: Attachment in Aid of Execution > Chapter 6: Sale of Attached Assets > Chapter 7: Enforcement Expenses
articles.text:
1. Without prejudice to paragraph (2) of this Article, the party subject to enforcement shall bear the
enforcement expenses, unless such expenses are attributed to another person; in such case, the
expenses shall be borne by such person pursuant to a court decision, which shall be appealable in
accordance with applicable procedures.
2. The party seeking enforcement shall bear the enforcement expenses if he terminates the
enforcement petition pursuant to Article 43(1)(e and f) of this Law, unless he agrees otherwise
with the party subject to enforcement.
3. Without prejudice to paragraph (1) of this Article, the enforcement expenses shall be paid by the
party subject to enforcement. If he refuses, the party seeking enforcement or any other party with
interest from among the enforcement parties may make such payment. Failure to pay such
expenses shall result in a stay of the enforcement proceedings provided for in this Law.

articles.label: Article 33
articles.chapter: Part 4: Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 1: Registration of Enforcement Petitions and Issuance of Writs of Execution > Chapter 2: Disclosure of Assets > Chapter 3: Compulsory Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 4: Asset Tracing > Chapter 5: Attachment in Aid of Execution > Chapter 6: Sale of Attached Assets > Chapter 7: Enforcement Expenses > Chapter 8: Deposit and Distribution of Enforcement Proceeds
articles.text:
1. The Ministry shall open bank accounts and maintain safe-deposit boxes for enforcement purposes.
The deposit and disbursement of enforcement proceeds, as well as the management of bank
accounts and safe-deposit boxes, shall be in accordance with the controls and procedures specified
in the Regulations.
2. The Regulations shall, in coordination with the Saudi Central Bank, specify the provisions and
procedures for the participation of banks and similar institutions in enforcement proceedings.

articles.label: Article 34
articles.chapter: Part 4: Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 1: Registration of Enforcement Petitions and Issuance of Writs of Execution > Chapter 2: Disclosure of Assets > Chapter 3: Compulsory Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 4: Asset Tracing > Chapter 5: Attachment in Aid of Execution > Chapter 6: Sale of Attached Assets > Chapter 7: Enforcement Expenses > Chapter 8: Deposit and Distribution of Enforcement Proceeds
articles.text:
If enforcement proceeds are sufficient to satisfy the amounts owed to the attaching parties and persons
deemed parties in enforcement proceedings pursuant to the provisions of this Law, the court shall
order the distribution of such proceeds among such parties in accordance with the Regulations.

articles.label: Article 35
articles.chapter: Part 4: Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 1: Registration of Enforcement Petitions and Issuance of Writs of Execution > Chapter 2: Disclosure of Assets > Chapter 3: Compulsory Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 4: Asset Tracing > Chapter 5: Attachment in Aid of Execution > Chapter 6: Sale of Attached Assets > Chapter 7: Enforcement Expenses > Chapter 8: Deposit and Distribution of Enforcement Proceeds
articles.text:
If enforcement proceeds are not sufficient to satisfy the amounts owed to the attaching parties and to
persons deemed parties in enforcement proceedings pursuant to the provisions of this Law, the court
shall proceed as follows:
1. If the attaching parties and persons deemed parties in the proceedings reach an amicable settlement
for the distribution of the proceeds, the court shall enter such settlement into the minutes and order
the distribution be made accordingly.
2. If the attaching parties and persons deemed parties in the proceedings fail to reach an amicable
settlement for the distribution of the proceeds, the court shall order such distribution be carried
out, provided that priority is given to privileged debts over all other debts in accordance with
applicable statutory provisions and the controls specified in the Regulations. The proceeds
distribution order shall be appealable in accordance with applicable procedures.

articles.label: Article 36
articles.chapter: Part 4: Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 1: Registration of Enforcement Petitions and Issuance of Writs of Execution > Chapter 2: Disclosure of Assets > Chapter 3: Compulsory Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 4: Asset Tracing > Chapter 5: Attachment in Aid of Execution > Chapter 6: Sale of Attached Assets > Chapter 7: Enforcement Expenses > Chapter 8: Deposit and Distribution of Enforcement Proceeds > Chapter 9: Direct Enforcement
articles.text:
If enforcement involves an act or omission of an act and the party subject to enforcement fails to
comply within five business days from the date of service or publication of the writ of execution in
accordance with Article 14 of this Law, the following compulsory enforcement measures shall be
carried out:
1. The court shall promptly order the competent force to carry out all necessary enforcement
proceedings, except for actions that must be performed by the party subject to enforcement.
2. The court shall, when necessary, promptly request the competent authority to effect fulfillment of
the right underlying the enforcement document.
3. If enforcement cannot be carried out by the competent force or the competent authority, or if the
party subject to enforcement fails to perform any of the actions required for enforcement, the
following compulsory enforcement measures shall be carried out:
a) The court shall, upon a petition by the party seeking enforcement, order that a travel ban be
placed on the party subject to enforcement in accordance with Article 19 of this Law.
b) The court shall impose against the party subject to enforcement a fine not exceeding ten
thousand riyals for each day of delay beyond the date set for completion of enforcement,
provided that such fine does not exceed the limit prescribed in the Regulations. The court may
waive the fine or part thereof if said party fulfills his obligation. The total amount of the fine
shall devolve to the State treasury.
The Regulations shall specify the controls and procedures necessary for the implementation of this
Article, including the controls and procedures for eviction and for disposal of movables in the
property, if not collected by their owner.

articles.label: Article 37
articles.chapter: Part 4: Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 1: Registration of Enforcement Petitions and Issuance of Writs of Execution > Chapter 2: Disclosure of Assets > Chapter 3: Compulsory Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 4: Asset Tracing > Chapter 5: Attachment in Aid of Execution > Chapter 6: Sale of Attached Assets > Chapter 7: Enforcement Expenses > Chapter 8: Deposit and Distribution of Enforcement Proceeds > Chapter 9: Direct Enforcement
articles.text:
1. If 30 business days lapse from the date of carrying out any of the compulsory enforcement
measures provided for in Article 36 of this Law and the party subject to enforcement fails to fulfill
his obligation, the court shall, upon a petition by the party seeking enforcement, order his
imprisonment for a term not exceeding 180 days to compel compliance therewith, renewable for
an additional term upon a petition by the party seeking enforcement.
2. A party subject to enforcement may not be imprisoned pursuant to paragraph (1) of this Article if
he is under 18 years of age, if it is established by a certified medical report that he suffers from an
illness that renders him unfit for imprisonment, if such party is a pregnant woman or a mother
whose child is under two years of age, or if such party is an ascendant or descendant of the party
seeking enforcement.
3. Persons imprisoned pursuant to paragraph (1) of this Article shall be housed separately from
inmates convicted in criminal cases.
4. Completion of the imprisonment sentence in accordance with paragraph (1) of this Article shall
not discharge the obligation underlying an enforcement document.

articles.label: Article 38
articles.chapter: Part 4: Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 1: Registration of Enforcement Petitions and Issuance of Writs of Execution > Chapter 2: Disclosure of Assets > Chapter 3: Compulsory Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 4: Asset Tracing > Chapter 5: Attachment in Aid of Execution > Chapter 6: Sale of Attached Assets > Chapter 7: Enforcement Expenses > Chapter 8: Deposit and Distribution of Enforcement Proceeds > Chapter 9: Direct Enforcement > Chapter 10: Enforcement in Family Matters
articles.text:
1. Enforcement documents in family matters shall be executed in the manner prescribed by this Law
and the Regulations.
2. The Regulations shall specify enforcement proceedings in family matters involving periodic
payments.

articles.label: Article 39
articles.chapter: Part 4: Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 1: Registration of Enforcement Petitions and Issuance of Writs of Execution > Chapter 2: Disclosure of Assets > Chapter 3: Compulsory Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 4: Asset Tracing > Chapter 5: Attachment in Aid of Execution > Chapter 6: Sale of Attached Assets > Chapter 7: Enforcement Expenses > Chapter 8: Deposit and Distribution of Enforcement Proceeds > Chapter 9: Direct Enforcement > Chapter 10: Enforcement in Family Matters
articles.text:
1. An enforcement document relating to custody and visitation shall be carried out by compulsion, if
warranted, even if this requires resorting to the competent force and forcibly entering homes.
Enforcement of such document shall be repeated if necessary.
2. Direct enforcement provisions shall apply to non-complying parties in family matters in
accordance with the controls specified in the Regulations; such controls shall take into account the
nature of family matters and the circumstances of enforcement.

articles.label: Article 40
articles.chapter: Part 4: Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 1: Registration of Enforcement Petitions and Issuance of Writs of Execution > Chapter 2: Disclosure of Assets > Chapter 3: Compulsory Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 4: Asset Tracing > Chapter 5: Attachment in Aid of Execution > Chapter 6: Sale of Attached Assets > Chapter 7: Enforcement Expenses > Chapter 8: Deposit and Distribution of Enforcement Proceeds > Chapter 9: Direct Enforcement > Chapter 10: Enforcement in Family Matters
articles.text:
The court shall, in executing an enforcement document regarding visitation of a person subject of
custody, take into consideration the interest of such person and the circumstances of enforcement.
The Regulations shall specify the provisions necessary for the implementation of this Article.

articles.label: Article 41
articles.chapter: Part 4: Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 1: Registration of Enforcement Petitions and Issuance of Writs of Execution > Chapter 2: Disclosure of Assets > Chapter 3: Compulsory Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 4: Asset Tracing > Chapter 5: Attachment in Aid of Execution > Chapter 6: Sale of Attached Assets > Chapter 7: Enforcement Expenses > Chapter 8: Deposit and Distribution of Enforcement Proceeds > Chapter 9: Direct Enforcement > Chapter 10: Enforcement in Family Matters > Chapter 11: Enforcement against Private Legal Personality
articles.text:
1. Direct enforcement provisions shall, in enforcement against private legal personality, apply to any
of its personnel who obstructs enforcement, in accordance with the controls and procedures
specified in the Regulations.
2. The Regulations shall, subject to paragraph (1) of this Article, specify the provisions and
proceedings for enforcement against the private legal personality in accordance with the provisions
of this Law and other relevant laws, and in a manner consistent with the nature of enforcement
against such personality.

articles.label: Article 42
articles.chapter: Part 4: Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 1: Registration of Enforcement Petitions and Issuance of Writs of Execution > Chapter 2: Disclosure of Assets > Chapter 3: Compulsory Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 4: Asset Tracing > Chapter 5: Attachment in Aid of Execution > Chapter 6: Sale of Attached Assets > Chapter 7: Enforcement Expenses > Chapter 8: Deposit and Distribution of Enforcement Proceeds > Chapter 9: Direct Enforcement > Chapter 10: Enforcement in Family Matters > Chapter 11: Enforcement against Private Legal Personality > Chapter 12: Termination of Enforcement Petition
articles.text:
The party seeking enforcement must, within the period prescribed in the Regulations, terminate his
petition upon satisfaction of the right underlying the enforcement document.

articles.label: Article 43
articles.chapter: Part 4: Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 1: Registration of Enforcement Petitions and Issuance of Writs of Execution > Chapter 2: Disclosure of Assets > Chapter 3: Compulsory Enforcement Proceedings > Chapter 4: Asset Tracing > Chapter 5: Attachment in Aid of Execution > Chapter 6: Sale of Attached Assets > Chapter 7: Enforcement Expenses > Chapter 8: Deposit and Distribution of Enforcement Proceeds > Chapter 9: Direct Enforcement > Chapter 10: Enforcement in Family Matters > Chapter 11: Enforcement against Private Legal Personality > Chapter 12: Termination of Enforcement Petition
articles.text:
1. An enforcement petition shall terminate in any of the following cases:
a) If the right underlying the enforcement document is satisfied.
b) If the court establishes that the party subject to enforcement has no assets. In such case, a
decision shall be issued to terminate the petition, and such decision shall be appealable in
accordance with applicable procedures.
c) If all enforcement proceedings provided for in this Law and the Regulations have been
exhausted, and the period prescribed for the enforcement petition has lapsed after the last
proceeding.
d) If enforcement is not feasible. In such case, a decision by the court shall be issued to terminate
the petition, and such decision shall be appealable in accordance with applicable procedures.
e) If the party seeking enforcement terminates his petition following an agreement with the party
subject to enforcement, or for any other reason.
f) If the party seeking enforcement discharges the party subject to enforcement from the
obligation underlying the enforcement document.
2. Termination of an enforcement petition under the cases provided for in paragraph (1)(b, c, d, and
e) of this Article shall not prejudice the creditor’s right to refile such petition in accordance with
the provisions of this Law if grounds for refiling exist.
3. The Regulations shall specify the controls and procedures necessary for the implementation of this
Article.

articles.label: Article 44
articles.chapter: Part 5: Enforcement Disputes and Appeals against Enforcement Proceedings
articles.text: All court orders and decisions shall be final except as otherwise provided for in this Law.

articles.label: Article 45
articles.chapter: Part 5: Enforcement Disputes and Appeals against Enforcement Proceedings
articles.text:
1. Without prejudice to Article 4(2) of this Law, any person with interest, whether a party to the
enforcement or otherwise, may file a claim contesting the validity of an enforcement document,
the conditions for its enforcement, or the jurisdiction of the court.
2. The court shall decide an enforcement dispute in accordance with the provisions governing
summary cases and the procedures specified in the Regulations.
3. The Council shall determine enforcement disputes in which rendered judgments are not
appealable.
4. Judgments rendered by appellate circuits regarding the judgments of enforcement disputes may
not be appealable by way of cassation.
5. Notwithstanding paragraph (4) of this Article, the Council may determine enforcement disputes
in which rendered judgments may be appealable by way of cassation.

articles.label: Article 46
articles.chapter: Part 5: Enforcement Disputes and Appeals against Enforcement Proceedings
articles.text:
1. Any person with interest may file a grievance against orders or decisions issued by the court, the
competent department, or a private sector entity regarding the enforcement proceedings specified
in the Regulations.
2. A grievance shall be decided by the chief judge of the court or the party the Council designates
within 10 business days from the day following the date on which access to a decision or order is
made available, in accordance with the Regulations. The chief judge or the party designated by
the Council, as the case may be, may stay enforcement of such order or decision if warranted,
pending issuance of a decision on the grievance; such stay shall entail staying all related
proceedings and time limits.
3. In all cases, the decision on the grievance provided for in this Article shall be final.

articles.label: Article 47
articles.chapter: Part 5: Enforcement Disputes and Appeals against Enforcement Proceedings
articles.text:
1. The existence of an enforcement dispute, a dispute relating to the merits of the claim underlying
the enforcement document, or a grievance against any enforcement proceeding shall not preclude
continuation of enforcement proceedings in accordance with the provisions of this Law and the
Regulations, unless the person considering such disputes or grievance decides otherwise.
2. A stay of enforcement proceedings shall entail staying all relating proceedings and time limits.

articles.label: Article 48
articles.chapter: Part 6: Penalties
articles.text:
1. Save for Article 57(1) of this Law, the competent court shall consider claims arising from the
application of the provisions of this Part and shall impose the penalties prescribed therein.
2. The competent authority in charge of investigation and prosecution shall undertake investigation
and prosecution before the competent court with respect to the offenses provided for in this Part.

articles.label: Article 49
articles.chapter: Part 6: Penalties
articles.text:
1. Without prejudice to relevant statutory provisions, detection and recording of offenses provided
for in this Part shall be carried out by officers from the Ministry or from any other public entity.
Said officers shall be appointed pursuant to a decision by the Minister and shall have the capacity
of preliminary investigation officers. The Regulations shall specify their powers, as well as the
procedures and controls necessary for performing their duties and exercising their powers.
2. Paragraph (1) of this Article shall not prejudice the power of the court to refer acts constituting
offenses under this Part directly to the competent authority in charge of investigation and
prosecution for completion of the necessary actions in accordance with relevant statutory
provisions.

articles.label: Article 50
articles.chapter: Part 6: Penalties
articles.text:
1. Imprisonment for a term not exceeding three years and a fine not exceeding one million riyals, or
either penalty, shall be imposed on any person who commits any of the following offenses:
a) Concealment or transfer of assets with the intent of preventing satisfaction of the right
underlying the enforcement document as provided for in the provisions of this Law.
b) Deliberate obstruction of enforcement by refusing to comply with the writ of execution,
refusing to disclose assets, filing a lawsuit to impede enforcement, disposing of assets subject
of enforcement after issuance of the writ of attachment, or failing to respond to the
interrogation, subject to the provisions of this Law.
c) Resistance of enforcement by threatening or assaulting, personally or through another person,
an official or an authorized person during execution of enforcement or by reason thereof,
committing any such acts against the party seeking enforcement by reason of enforcement, or
committing any other unlawful act with the intent of resisting enforcement.
d) Deliberate submission of misleading or incorrect information to the court or during enforcement
proceedings.
2. An accomplice in the commission of any of the offenses provided for in this Article shall be subject
to the penalty prescribed in paragraph (1) of this Article. A person shall be deemed an accomplice
if he knowingly agrees to, incites, or aids and abets in the commission of an offense and if the
offense is committed as a result of such agreement, incitement, or aiding and abetting.

articles.label: Article 51
articles.chapter: Part 6: Penalties
articles.text:
A public servant and any person of similar status who prevents or obstructs enforcement shall be
subject to imprisonment for a term not exceeding five years. Such act shall be deemed an offense
impinging upon integrity.

articles.label: Article 52
articles.chapter: Part 6: Penalties
articles.text:
1. Any debtor proven to have dissipated his assets, if such assets are substantial, shall be subject to
imprisonment for a term not exceeding 15 years, even if such debtor is established to be insolvent.
Such act shall constitute a major offense warranting detention.
2. The Public Prosecutor shall, upon coordination with the Ministry of Justice and the Ministry of
Finance, establish controls and standards for determining when assets are deemed substantial as
provided for in paragraph (1) of this Article, as per the types of debts and assets of debtors.

articles.label: Article 53
articles.chapter: Part 6: Penalties
articles.text:
Imprisonment for a term not exceeding three years and a fine not exceeding one hundred thousand
riyals, or either penalty, shall be imposed on:
1. the party seeking enforcement who petitions for a specific enforcement proceeding with the intent
of harming the party subject to enforcement, or who, with the intent of harming the party subject
to enforcement, delays termination of an enforcement petition after the right underlying the
enforcement document is satisfied;
2. a person authorized under the provisions of this Law to access information relating to the assets
of the party subject to enforcement who discloses such information without legal grounds; the
same penalty shall apply to any person who, without a judicial order, accesses such information;
3. any licensed enforcement service provider, or any of the subordinates thereof, breaching duties by
misappropriating assets or evading delivery or receipt of assets; and
4. the appraiser, sale agent, their subordinates, or any participant in auction sales, who deliberately
influences or manipulates prices.

articles.label: Article 54
articles.chapter: Part 6: Penalties
articles.text:
A parent or any other person who refuses, resists, or obstructs enforcement of a writ of execution
relating to custody, guardianship, or visitation shall be subject to imprisonment for a term not
exceeding 90 days and a fine not exceeding thirty thousand riyals, or to either penalty.

articles.label: Article 55
articles.chapter: Part 6: Penalties
articles.text:
If an act constituting an offense under this Part constitutes an offense under another law, the harsher
penalty shall be imposed.

articles.label: Article 56
articles.chapter: Part 6: Penalties
articles.text:
In case of repeating any of the offenses provided for in this Part, the prescribed penalty may be
doubled even if it entails exceeding the maximum limit, provided that it does not exceed double the
maximum limit. A person shall be deemed a repeat offender if he commits the same offense for which
a final judgment was rendered within three years from the date of such judgment.

articles.label: Article 57
articles.chapter: Part 6: Penalties
articles.text:
1. Without prejudice to any harsher penalty stipulated in any other law and absent a specific provision
in this Law, an enforcement service provider who violates any provisions of this Law, the
Regulations, or the Regulations for the Activities of Enforcement Service Providers shall be
subject to one or more of the following penalties:
a) A warning.
b) A fine not exceeding three hundred thousand riyals.
c) Suspension of the license for a period not exceeding one year.
d) Revocation of the license.
2. The Minister shall form a committee, or more, comprising at least three members, one of whom is
the chairman and among them is a legal advisor, to consider the violations referred to in paragraph
(1) of this Article and impose the penalties prescribed therein, according to the type, gravity, and
impact of the violation. Committee decisions must be approved by the Minister or his designee.
The Minister shall issue a decision determining the committee’s work rules and procedures and
the remuneration of its members.
3. A person against whom a decision is issued by the committee referred to in paragraph (2) of this
Article may file a grievance with the administrative court in accordance with the provisions of the
Law of Procedure before the Board of Grievances.

articles.label: Article 58
articles.chapter: Part 6: Penalties
articles.text:
1. The competent court or the committee referred to in Article 57(2) of this Law may, as the case
may be, include in its penalty decision or judgment a provision requiring publication of a summary
thereof at the expense of the convicted person or the violator, in a newspaper, or more, issued in
his area of residence or, if none exists, in the nearest area, or through any other appropriate means,
according to the type, gravity, and impact of the offense or violation. Such publication shall be
made after the judgment becomes final, the decision becomes unappealable due to the lapse of the
statutory period for filing grievances, or upon the issuance of a final ruling to dismiss the
grievance.
2. The competent court or the committee referred to in Article 57(2) of this Law may, as the case
may be, include in its judgment or penalty decision a provision requiring the violator to attend
certain correctional programs at his own expense.

articles.label: Article 59
articles.chapter: Part 7: Final Provisions
articles.text:
Absent a specific provision in this Law, the Law of Civil Procedure shall apply to the procedures and
disputes provided for in this Law, in a manner not inconsistent therewith.

articles.label: Article 60
articles.chapter: Part 7: Final Provisions
articles.text:
1. Except for the issuance of orders of imprisonment against the party subject to enforcement
compelling direct enforcement; orders banning travel outside the Kingdom; adjudication of
disputes and grievances; and the issuance of judgments, the enforcement proceedings provided for
in this Law and the Regulations may, pursuant to the Minister's decision, be assigned to the
competent department, the competent authority after coordination therewith, or the private sector.
2. A private sector entity to which an enforcement proceeding is assigned pursuant to paragraph (1)
of this Article must meet the following conditions:
a) The entity must be licensed in the Kingdom to engage in the activity subject of the assignment.
b) The entity must have the technical expertise and financial capacity necessary to carry out the
assignment, as determined by the Ministry.
c) The entity must not have a conflict of interest, whether actual or potential.
d) The entity must maintain confidentiality of any information to which it becomes privy by reason
of the assignment; such obligation shall survive the expiration of the assignment.
3. The Regulations shall specify the provisions and procedures necessary for the implementation of
paragraph (1) of this Article.

articles.label: Article 61
articles.chapter: Part 7: Final Provisions
articles.text:
1. The Ministry shall license and supervise enforcement service providers, including court-appointed
sale agents and receivers as well as service providers for asset tracing, asset recovery, and
enforcement of visitations in family matters, and other persons specified in the Regulations.
2. The Minister shall issue regulations governing the activities of enforcement service providers,
including their functions, licensing requirements and financial guarantees, qualifications and
duties, as well as the rules and procedures for detecting and recording violations committed
thereby, and the policies for determining their service fees.

articles.label: Article 62
articles.chapter: Part 7: Final Provisions
articles.text:
Approved electronic means shall be used for taking decisions or carrying out any of the enforcement
proceedings provided for in this Law and the Regulations. If the purpose of the decision or proceeding
can be achieved through approved modern technology methods, such methods shall be used. If,
however, enforcement through approved electronic means or approved modern technology methods
proves infeasible, ordinary means shall be used.

articles.label: Article 63
articles.chapter: Part 7: Final Provisions
articles.text:
The Ministry shall issue the procedural guidelines, decisions, and forms necessary for the
implementation of this Law and the Regulations.

articles.label: Article 64
articles.chapter: Part 7: Final Provisions
articles.text:
The Minister shall issue the Regulations within 180 days from the date of publication of this Law in
the Official Gazette. The Regulations shall enter into force from the date this Law enters into force.

articles.label: Article 65
articles.chapter: Part 7: Final Provisions
articles.text:
1. This Law shall supersede the Enforcement Law promulgated by Royal Decree No. M/53, dated
13/8/1433H, and its amendments, and shall repeal any provision conflicting therewith.
2. This Law shall enter into force 180 days from the date of its publication in the Official Gazette.
